name: Other Urologic Problems
shortDescription:
Not every urologic concern fits neatly into a single category. From pelvic organ prolapse to voiding dysfunction, urethral conditions, and other less common issues, RoMIUS Urology provides expert evaluation and treatment for the full range of women's urologic health concerns.
Whatever you're experiencing, we're here to help you find answers.
body:
What Falls Under "Other Urologic Problems"?

Urologic health is broad, and many women experience symptoms that don't fit into a single, well-defined category. This can include:

  • Pelvic organ prolapse (bladder, uterine, or vaginal)
  • Voiding dysfunction (difficulty starting, weak stream, incomplete emptying)
  • Urethral diverticulum
  • Urethral stricture
  • Overactive bladder (OAB)
  • Stress urinary incontinence
  • Neurogenic bladder
  • Congenital or structural urologic abnormalities
  • Post-surgical or post-radiation urologic complications
  • Fistulas (bladder, urethral, or vaginal)
  • Sexual dysfunction with a urologic component

Because these conditions vary widely in cause and presentation, an individualized evaluation is the first step toward the right treatment.

Our Approach to Evaluation

RoMIUS Urology takes a thorough, patient-centered approach to identifying the source of your symptoms:

  • Detailed history and physical examination
  • Urinalysis and urine culture
  • Bladder diary and symptom tracking
  • Urodynamic testing when indicated
  • Cystoscopy when indicated
  • Imaging (ultrasound, CT, or MRI) as needed
  • Pelvic floor assessment
  • Review of prior surgeries, deliveries, or pelvic trauma

This comprehensive workup allows us to pinpoint the underlying issue, even when symptoms are unusual or difficult to categorize.

Pelvic Organ Prolapse

Prolapse occurs when pelvic organs — the bladder, uterus, or rectum — shift from their normal position due to weakened pelvic support. Symptoms can include:

  • A sensation of pelvic pressure or bulging
  • Difficulty emptying the bladder
  • Urinary leakage
  • Discomfort during activity or intercourse

Treatment options range from pelvic floor physical therapy and pessary fitting to surgical repair, depending on severity and patient goals.

Voiding Dysfunction and Overactive Bladder

Difficulty with normal bladder emptying, or the opposite — urgency and frequency without infection — can significantly affect daily life. We offer:

  • Behavioral and dietary modification
  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Medications for bladder relaxation or emptying
  • Botox® for refractory overactive bladder
  • Sacral neuromodulation (InterStim®) for severe cases
  • Clean intermittent catheterization training when needed

Structural and Post-Surgical Concerns

Some women develop urologic issues following childbirth, prior pelvic surgery, or radiation treatment — including strictures, fistulas, or scar-related complications. We coordinate closely with gynecology, colorectal, and pelvic floor specialists to manage these complex cases with a team-based approach.

Why Women Choose RoMIUS Urology

  • Expertise across the full spectrum of women's urologic conditions
  • Willingness to investigate symptoms that don't fit a standard diagnosis
  • Advanced diagnostic tools, including urodynamics
  • Strong collaboration with pelvic floor therapists and other specialists
  • Compassionate, unhurried evaluations
  • Personalized treatment plans, from conservative to surgical options
